access_key.description: RadosGW access key. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable.

endpoint.description: RadosGW endpoint URL. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

root_ca_certificate.description: PEM-encoded root CA certificate content to use for TLS verification. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ROOT_CA_CERTIFICATE` environment variable.

root_ca_certificate_file.description: Path to a PEM-encoded root CA certificate file to use for TLS verification. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_ROOT_CA_CERTIFICATE_FILE` environment variable.

secret_key.description: RadosGW secret key. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_SECRET_KEY` environment variable.

tls_insecure_skip_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification for HTTPS connections. This is useful when connecting to RadosGW with self-signed certificates or certificates signed by an untrusted CA. Has no effect on plain HTTP connections. Can be set via the `RADOSGW_TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY` environment variable. Default is `false`.

block.description:
Terraform provider for managing Ceph RADOS Gateway (RadosGW) resources via Admin and S3 APIs.

## Required User Capabilities

The RadosGW user configured in this provider requires specific capabilities to manage different resources:

| Capability | Resources |
|------------|-----------|
| `users=*` | `radosgw_iam_user`, `radosgw_iam_subuser`, `radosgw_iam_access_key`, `radosgw_iam_user_caps`, `radosgw_iam_quota`, `radosgw_iam_user`, `radosgw_iam_users` |
| `buckets=*` | `radosgw_s3_bucket`, `radosgw_s3_bucket_link`, `radosgw_s3_bucket_acl`, `radosgw_s3_bucket_policy`, `radosgw_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration` |
| `oidc-provider=*` | `radosgw_iam_openid_connect_provider` |
| `roles=*` | `radosgw_iam_role`, `radosgw_iam_role_policy`, `radosgw_iam_roles` |
| `metadata=*` | `radosgw_iam_users` |

To grant all required capabilities to a user:

```bash
radosgw-admin caps add --uid=admin --caps="buckets=*;metadata=*;oidc-provider=*;roles=*;users=*"
```

access_key.description: The access key. For S3 keys: if not provided, it will be auto-generated. For Swift keys: this is computed as `user_id:subuser`. Changing this value will force resource replacement.

generated.description: Whether the key was auto-generated (true) or user-specified (false). Only applicable for S3 keys.

id.description: The resource identifier. For S3 keys: the `access_key`. For Swift keys: `user_id:subuser`.

key_type.description: The type of key. Valid values: `s3` (default), `swift`.

secret_key.description: The secret key. If not provided, it will be auto-generated. Changing this value will update the key in place.

subuser.description: The subuser name (without the user prefix). Required for Swift keys, not used for S3 keys.

user_id.description: The user ID for which to create the key.

block.description:
Manages an IAM access key for S3 or Swift access in RadosGW.

**S3 keys:** Multiple access keys per user are supported. Keys are identified by `access_key`.

**Swift keys:** Only one access key per subuser is supported. Creating a new key replaces the existing one. Requires a `subuser` attribute.

~> **Note:** Managing multiple S3 keys per user requires Ceph Squid (19.x) or higher. Older versions (Reef 18.x) may have issues with key deletion when multiple keys exist.

allow_updates.description: Whether to allow in-place updates for `client_id_list` and `thumbprint_list`. When `true` (default), changes will be applied in-place. When `false`, changes to these attributes will destroy and recreate the provider. ~> **Note:** In-place updates require Ceph Tentacle (20.x). On older versions, set to `false`.

arn.description: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the OIDC provider. Format: `arn:aws:iam:::oidc-provider/<url>` (URL portion excludes protocol).

client_id_list.description: List of client IDs (also known as audiences) that are allowed to authenticate with this provider. These values correspond to the `aud` claim in OIDC tokens.

thumbprint_list.description: List of certificate thumbprints for the OpenID Connect provider's IDP certificate(s). Each thumbprint is a hex-encoded SHA-1 hash (40 characters). A maximum of 5 thumbprints are allowed.

url.description: URL of the identity provider. This value corresponds to the `iss` claim in OIDC tokens. Must include the protocol (`http://` or `https://`). The full URL is stored and used when RadosGW contacts the OIDC provider, but the protocol is stripped when constructing the ARN.

block.description:
Manages an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider in RadosGW. This resource allows you to establish trust between RadosGW and an external OpenID Connect provider for federated authentication.

~> **Note:** RadosGW normalizes OIDC provider URLs by stripping the protocol (`http://`, `https://`) when constructing ARNs. This means `http://example.com` and `https://example.com` would result in the **same** ARN `arn:aws:iam:::oidc-provider/example.com`. You cannot create separate providers for the same domain with different protocols. Changing the protocol in the URL triggers resource replacement.

enabled.description: Whether the quota is enabled. Default: `true`.

max_objects.description: Maximum number of objects. Use `-1` for unlimited. Default: `-1`.

max_size.description: Maximum size in bytes. Use `-1` for unlimited. Default: `-1`.

type.description:
The quota type:
  - `user`: Total quota across all user's buckets combined
  - `bucket`: Per-bucket quota applied to each bucket the user owns

user_id.description: The user ID to configure quotas for. Plain user IDs, tenant-qualified IDs (`tenant$user_id`), and `radosgw_iam_user.user_id` references are supported. A plain ID is used directly when a non-tenant user with that ID exists. If no direct user exists, a local tenant user ID is resolved only when it uniquely matches one tenant user. When both a global user and tenant user share the same local ID, or multiple tenants share that local ID, use `radosgw_iam_user.id` or the tenant-qualified `tenant$user_id` form.

block.description:
Manages user-level quotas in RadosGW. This resource configures storage and object limits for a user.

**Important:** This resource manages quotas at the **user level**, not individual bucket quotas. There are two types:

- **User quota** (`type = "user"`): Sets the total storage limit across ALL buckets owned by the user. When exceeded, the user cannot store more data in any of their buckets.

- **Bucket quota** (`type = "bucket"`): Sets a per-bucket limit that applies to EACH bucket owned by the user. Every bucket the user owns will have this same quota applied.

Upon deletion, the quota is disabled (not removed, as quotas are properties of users).

~> **Note:** Account-level quotas are not yet supported by the go-ceph library. Only user-level quotas are currently available.

arn.description: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the role.

assume_role_policy.description: The trust relationship policy document (in JSON format) that grants an entity permission to assume the role. Use `jsonencode()` or the `radosgw_iam_policy_document` data source to generate this.

create_date.description: Date and time when the role was created.

description.description: A description of the role. Maximum 1000 characters. ~> **Note:** This field is stored in state but may not be returned by the RadosGW API on older Ceph versions (Reef 18.x). The provider preserves the configured value in this case.

max_session_duration.description: Maximum session duration (in seconds) for the role. Default is 3600 (1 hour). Valid values: 3600-43200 (1-12 hours).

name.description: The name of the role. Must be unique and can contain up to 64 characters. Valid characters: alphanumeric characters, plus (+), equals (=), comma (,), period (.), at (@), underscore (_), and hyphen (-).

path.description: The path to the role. Default is `/`. Paths must begin and end with `/`.

tags.description: Map of tags to assign to the role.

block.description: Manages an IAM role in RadosGW. Roles define a set of permissions for making service requests and can be assumed by trusted entities using STS AssumeRole or AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.

id.description: The unique identifier for this policy. Format: `role:policy_name`.

name.description: The name of the policy. Must be unique within the role.

policy.description: The policy document (in JSON format). Use `jsonencode()` or the `radosgw_iam_policy_document` data source to generate this.

role.description: The name of the role to associate the policy with.

block.description: Manages an inline IAM policy for a RadosGW role. Inline policies are embedded directly in the role. For managed policies that can be attached to multiple roles, consider using a separate policy resource.

access.description: Access level for the subuser. Valid values: `read`, `write`, `read-write`, `full-control`. Default: `read`.

id.description: The full subuser ID in the format `{user_id}:{subuser}`.

secret_key.description: The auto-generated Swift secret key. This is the initial key created by Ceph when the subuser is created. ~> **Note:** For production use, consider managing keys explicitly with the `radosgw_iam_access_key` resource for rotation and lifecycle management. This field is computed (read-only) and will not detect or track external key changes.

subuser.description: The subuser name (without the parent user prefix). The full subuser ID will be `{user_id}:{subuser}`.

block.description:
Manages a RadosGW subuser. Subusers are additional identities under a parent user used for Swift API access. The full subuser ID has the format `{user_id}:{subuser}`. ~> **Note:** Ceph automatically generates one Swift secret key when creating a subuser (only one Swift key is allowed per subuser). Keys can be managed separately or replaced later using the `radosgw_iam_access_key` resource with `key_type = "swift"`.

~> **Note:** Creating multiple subusers for a single user requires Ceph Squid (19.x) or higher. Older versions (Reef 18.x) may have issues with multiple subuser creation.

default_placement.description: The default placement for the user's buckets. Note: Once set, this field cannot be cleared, only changed to a different value.

default_storage_class.description: The default storage class for the user's objects.

display_name.description: The display name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user. Note: Once set, this field cannot be cleared, only changed to a different value.

id.description: The tenant-qualified RGW user ID. For tenant users this is `tenant$user_id`; for non-tenant users this matches `user_id`.

max_buckets.description: The maximum number of buckets the user can own. Default is 1000.

op_mask.description: The operation mask for the user. Default is 'read, write, delete'.

suspended.description: Whether the user is suspended. Default is false.

tenant.description: The tenant to which the user belongs. Cannot be modified after creation.

user_id.description: The local user ID. For tenant users, this remains the user name without the tenant prefix; use `id` when another resource needs the tenant-qualified RGW user ID.

block.description: Manages a RadosGW user.

perm.description: The permission level. Valid values: `*` (full access), `read`, `write`. Note: Ceph converts `read` + `write` to `*` internally.

caps.description: Set of capabilities to grant to the user. Each capability has a type and permission level.

user_id.description: The user ID to manage capabilities for.

block.description:
Manages RadosGW user capabilities. Capabilities control administrative permissions for a user.

Capabilities are defined as a set of type/permission pairs. Each capability type can only appear once in the set.
Use `perm = "*"` for full access instead of specifying separate read and write entries.

The provider automatically:
- Sorts capabilities alphabetically by type to prevent unnecessary changes
- Validates that no duplicate capability types are specified

On deletion, all specified capabilities are removed from the user.

acl.description: The canned ACL of the bucket. This is a read-only attribute. To manage bucket ACLs, use the `radosgw_s3_bucket_acl` resource.

bucket.description: The name of the bucket. Must be unique within the RadosGW cluster. Bucket names must be between 3 and 63 characters, start with a lowercase letter or number, and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.

enabled.description: Whether the bucket quota is enabled.

max_objects.description: Maximum number of objects. -1 means unlimited.

max_size.description: Maximum size in bytes. -1 means unlimited.

bucket_quota.description: Quota settings for this specific bucket. Managed via the Admin API.

creation_time.description: The creation time of the bucket in RFC3339 format.

data_extra_pool.description: The RADOS pool for storing extra object data (e.g., multipart uploads).

data_pool.description: The RADOS pool for storing object data.

index_pool.description: The RADOS pool for storing the bucket index.

explicit_placement.description: Explicit placement configuration showing the RADOS pools used for the bucket.

force_destroy.description: Whether to delete all objects in the bucket when destroying the resource. Uses the Admin API with purge-objects option. Default is false.

id.description: The unique identifier of the bucket assigned by RadosGW.

marker.description: The internal bucket marker used by RadosGW.

num_shards.description: The number of shards for the bucket index.

object_lock_enabled.description: Whether S3 Object Lock is enabled for the bucket. Can only be set at creation time and cannot be modified afterwards.

owner.description: The user ID of the bucket owner. This is a read-only attribute reflecting the current owner. The bucket is owned by the user whose credentials are used in the provider. To transfer ownership, use the `radosgw_s3_bucket_link` resource.

placement_rule.description: The placement rule for the bucket, determining which pools store the bucket's data.

tenant.description: The tenant the bucket belongs to. Can only be set at creation time. When set, the bucket is created with the tenant prefix.

versioning.description: The versioning state of the bucket. Valid values: 'off', 'enabled', 'suspended'. Default is 'off'.

zonegroup.description: The zonegroup ID where the bucket is located.

block.description: Manages an S3 bucket in Ceph RadosGW. This resource creates buckets via the S3 API and manages bucket configuration through both S3 and Admin APIs.

acl.description: The canned ACL to apply to the bucket. Valid values: `private`, `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `authenticated-read`.

bucket.description: The name of the bucket to apply the ACL to.

block.description:
Manages the ACL (Access Control List) for an S3 bucket in Ceph RadosGW. This resource allows you to set canned ACLs on buckets and tracks drift when the ACL is changed outside of Terraform.

~> **Important:** This resource can only manage ACLs for buckets owned by the user configured in the provider. The S3 API restricts ACL operations to the bucket owner only - even admin credentials cannot manage ACLs on buckets owned by other users. If you need to manage ACLs on buckets with different owners, you must use separate provider configurations (aliases) with each owner's credentials.

~> **Note:** When destroying this resource, the bucket ACL is reset to `private`.

bucket.description: The name of the bucket to apply the lifecycle configuration to.

id.description: Unique identifier for the rule. Maximum 255 characters.

status.description: Whether the rule is currently being applied. Valid values: `Enabled`, `Disabled`.

days_after_initiation.description: Number of days after initiating a multipart upload when it should be aborted.

block.description: Specifies when incomplete multipart uploads are aborted.

days.description: Number of days after object creation when the object expires.

expired_object_delete_marker.description: Whether to remove expired object delete markers. Only valid for versioned buckets.

block.description: Specifies when objects expire (are deleted).

prefix.description: Object key prefix that identifies one or more objects to which the rule applies.

tags.description: Map of tags that objects must have to match.

block.description: A logical AND to combine multiple filter conditions. Use this to apply a rule to objects that match all specified conditions.
A tag to filter objects. The rule applies only to objects that have the specified tag.
Filter that identifies the objects to which the rule applies. If not specified, the rule applies to all objects in the bucket.

newer_noncurrent_versions.description: Number of noncurrent versions to retain. If specified, the rule only applies after this many noncurrent versions exist.

noncurrent_days.description: Number of days after an object becomes noncurrent when it expires.

block.description: Specifies when noncurrent object versions expire. Only valid for versioned buckets.

newer_noncurrent_versions.description: Number of noncurrent versions to retain before transitioning.

noncurrent_days.description: Number of days after an object becomes noncurrent when the transition occurs.

storage_class.description: The storage class to transition noncurrent versions to.

block.description: Specifies when noncurrent object versions transition to a different storage class. Only valid for versioned buckets.

days.description: Number of days after object creation when the transition occurs.

storage_class.description: The storage class to transition objects to. The available storage classes depend on your RadosGW configuration.

block.description: Specifies when objects transition to a different storage class.
A lifecycle rule for the bucket. At least one rule is required.

Manages lifecycle configuration for an S3 bucket in RadosGW.

Lifecycle rules allow you to define actions that RadosGW applies to objects during their lifetime. Common use cases include:
- Expiring (deleting) objects after a certain number of days
- Transitioning objects to different storage classes
- Cleaning up incomplete multipart uploads
- Managing noncurrent versions in versioned buckets

~> **Note:** RadosGW supports a subset of Amazon S3 lifecycle features. Some advanced filtering options (like object size filtering) may not be available. See the [Ceph documentation](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/) for details.

~> **Important:** Only one lifecycle configuration can exist per bucket. This resource will replace any existing lifecycle configuration.

bucket.description: The name of the bucket to link. The bucket must already exist.

bucket_id.description: The unique bucket ID assigned by RadosGW.

new_bucket_name.description: Optional new name for the bucket. Use this to rename the bucket during the link operation.

uid.description: The user ID to link the bucket to. This user will become the bucket owner.

unlink_to_uid.description: The user ID to link the bucket to when this resource is destroyed. If not set, the bucket will be unlinked from the user but remain in the system.

block.description:
Manages bucket ownership in RadosGW by linking a bucket to a specified user.

This resource links an existing bucket to a user, unlinking it from any previous owner. It is primarily useful for:
- Transferring bucket ownership between users
- Moving buckets from one tenant to another
- Renaming buckets during the link operation

On destruction, the bucket can optionally be linked to a different user (via `unlink_to_uid`), or simply unlinked from the current user.

~> **Note:** The bucket must already exist. This resource does not create buckets, only manages ownership. The `owner` attribute on `radosgw_s3_bucket` is read-only, so this resource can be used alongside it without conflicts.

~> **Important:** When transferring bucket ownership, the `radosgw_s3_bucket_acl` and `radosgw_s3_bucket_policy` resources can only be managed by the bucket owner. If you transfer ownership to a different user, you will need separate provider credentials (aliases) to manage those resources.

bucket.description: The name of the S3 bucket to configure notifications for.

events.description:
The S3 event types that trigger notifications. Supported events include:
  - `s3:ObjectCreated:*` — all object creation events
  - `s3:ObjectCreated:Put`
  - `s3:ObjectCreated:Post`
  - `s3:ObjectCreated:Copy`
  - `s3:ObjectCreated:CompleteMultipartUpload`
  - `s3:ObjectRemoved:*` — all object removal events
  - `s3:ObjectRemoved:Delete`
  - `s3:ObjectRemoved:DeleteMarkerCreated`
  - `s3:ObjectLifecycle:Expiration:*` — lifecycle expiration (Ceph extension)
  - `s3:ObjectLifecycle:Expiration:Current`
  - `s3:ObjectLifecycle:Expiration:NonCurrent`
  - `s3:ObjectLifecycle:Expiration:DeleteMarker`
  - `s3:ObjectLifecycle:Expiration:AbortMultipartUpload`
  - `s3:ObjectLifecycle:Transition:Current`
  - `s3:ObjectLifecycle:Transition:NonCurrent`
  - `s3:ObjectSynced:*` — multisite sync events (Ceph extension)
  - `s3:ObjectRestore:*` — object restore events

filter_prefix.description: Object key name prefix to filter notifications. Only events for objects whose keys start with this prefix will trigger a notification.

filter_suffix.description: Object key name suffix to filter notifications. Only events for objects whose keys end with this suffix will trigger a notification.

id.description: Unique identifier for the notification configuration. If not specified, a random ID is generated.

topic_arn.description: The ARN of the SNS topic to publish notifications to. The topic must already exist.

block.description: Notification configuration for an SNS topic destination. Multiple `topic` blocks can be specified to send different events or filtered subsets of events to different topics.

Manages S3 bucket notification configuration in RadosGW. Bucket notifications send event information to SNS topic endpoints when specific events occur on the bucket.

~> **Note:** S3 buckets only support a single notification configuration. Declaring multiple `radosgw_s3_bucket_notification` resources for the same bucket will cause a perpetual difference in configuration. Use multiple `topic` blocks within a single resource to configure multiple notifications.

~> **Note:** RadosGW only supports SNS topic destinations for bucket notifications. SQS, Lambda, and EventBridge destinations are not supported.

bucket.description: The name of the bucket to which the policy will be applied.

id.description: The bucket name (used as the resource ID).

policy.description: The policy document in JSON format. Use `jsonencode()` or the `radosgw_iam_policy_document` data source to generate this.

block.description:
Attaches a policy to an S3 bucket in RadosGW. Only one policy can be attached to a bucket at a time.

Bucket policies provide access control for S3 buckets and their objects. They use the same policy language as IAM policies
but are attached directly to buckets rather than users or roles.

~> **Note:** Bucket policies in RadosGW support a subset of Amazon S3 policy features. See the
[Ceph RadosGW Bucket Policies documentation](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/bucketpolicy/) for supported actions and conditions.

~> **Important:** Destroying this resource will delete the bucket policy. The bucket itself will remain.

key.description: The object key name to use when a 4XX class error occurs.

block.description: The name of the error document for the website.

suffix.description: A suffix that is appended to a request that is for a directory on the website endpoint. For example, if the suffix is `index.html` and you make a request to `samplebucket/images/`, the data that is returned will be for the object with the key name `images/index.html`. The suffix must not be empty and must not include a slash character.

block.description: The name of the index document for the website. Required if `redirect_all_requests_to` is not specified.

host_name.description: Name of the host where requests are redirected.

protocol.description: Protocol to use when redirecting requests. The default is the protocol that is used in the original request. Valid values: `http`, `https`.

block.description: Redirect behavior for every request to this bucket's website endpoint. Conflicts with `index_document`, `error_document`, and `routing_rule`.

http_error_code_returned_equals.description: The HTTP error code when the redirect is applied. If specified with `key_prefix_equals`, then both conditions must be true for the redirect to be applied.

key_prefix_equals.description: The object key name prefix when the redirect is applied. If specified with `http_error_code_returned_equals`, then both conditions must be true for the redirect to be applied.

block.description: A condition that must be met for the specified redirect to apply.

host_name.description: The host name to use in the redirect request.

http_redirect_code.description: The HTTP redirect code to use on the response.

protocol.description: Protocol to use when redirecting requests. The default is the protocol that is used in the original request. Valid values: `http`, `https`.

replace_key_prefix_with.description: The object key prefix to use in the redirect request. For example, to redirect requests for all pages with prefix `docs/` to `documents/`, set `key_prefix_equals` to `docs/` in the condition and `replace_key_prefix_with` to `/documents` in the redirect. Cannot be specified with `replace_key_with`.

replace_key_with.description: The specific object key to use in the redirect request. For example, redirect request to `error.html`. Cannot be specified with `replace_key_prefix_with`.

block.description: Redirect information. You can redirect requests to another host, to another page, or with another protocol.
A list of rules that define when a redirect is applied and the redirect behavior. Conflicts with `redirect_all_requests_to`.

Manages an S3 bucket website configuration in RadosGW. This resource configures a bucket to serve static website content.

When configured, the bucket content is accessible through the RadosGW S3 website endpoint: `http://<bucket>.<rgw-host>:<port>`.

~> **Note:** S3 buckets only support a single website configuration. Declaring multiple `radosgw_s3_bucket_website_configuration` resources for the same bucket will cause conflicts.

~> **Note:** When this resource is destroyed, the website configuration is removed from the bucket.

amqp_ack_level.description: AMQP acknowledgement level. Valid values: `none`, `broker`, `routable`. Default is `broker`.

amqp_exchange.description: The AMQP exchange name. The exchange must exist and be able to route messages based on topics. Required for AMQP endpoints.

arn.description: The ARN (Amazon Resource Name) of the topic in the format `arn:aws:sns:<zone-group>:<tenant>:<topic>`.

ca_location.description: Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate file for authenticating the broker when using SSL.

cloudevents.description: Whether HTTP headers should include attributes according to the [S3 CloudEvents Spec](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/adapters/aws-s3.md). Only applicable to HTTP endpoints. Default is `false`.

kafka_ack_level.description: Kafka acknowledgement level. Valid values: `none`, `broker`. Default is `broker`.

kafka_brokers.description: Comma-separated list of Kafka brokers in `host:port` format. Added to the Kafka URI to support Kafka clusters.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retries before expiring a notification. Only applicable when `persistent` is `true`. Zero means infinite. Not returned by `GetTopicAttributes` on Ceph Reef (18.x); the configured value is preserved in state.

mechanism.description: SASL mechanism for Kafka authentication. Supported values: `PLAIN`, `SCRAM-SHA-256`, `SCRAM-SHA-512`, `GSSAPI`, `OAUTHBEARER`. Default is `PLAIN`.

name.description: The name of the topic. Must be unique per tenant. Changing the name forces creation of a new topic.

opaque_data.description: Opaque data set in the topic configuration and added to all notifications triggered by the topic.

password.description: Password for broker authentication. Overrides the password in the endpoint URI if both are provided. Must be transmitted over HTTPS.

persistent.description: Whether notifications to this endpoint are persistent (asynchronous). Persistent notifications are committed to storage and retried until delivered. Default is `false`.

push_endpoint.description:
The URI of the endpoint to send push notifications to. Supported protocols:
  - HTTP: `http[s]://<fqdn>[:<port>]`
  - AMQP 0.9.1: `amqp[s]://[<user>:<password>@]<fqdn>[:<port>][/<vhost>]`
  - Kafka: `kafka://[<user>:<password>@]<fqdn>[:<port>]`

retry_sleep_duration.description: Time in seconds between notification delivery retries. Only applicable when `persistent` is `true`. Zero means no delay. Not returned by `GetTopicAttributes` on Ceph Reef (18.x); the configured value is preserved in state.

time_to_live.description: Maximum time in seconds to retain notifications. Only applicable when `persistent` is `true`. Zero means infinite. Not returned by `GetTopicAttributes` on Ceph Reef (18.x); the configured value is preserved in state.

use_ssl.description: Whether a secure connection is used to connect to the broker. Applicable to Kafka and AMQP endpoints. Default is `false`.

user.description: The name of the user that created the topic. Not returned by Ceph Reef (18.x).

user_name.description: Username for broker authentication. Overrides the user in the endpoint URI if both are provided. Must be transmitted over HTTPS.

verify_ssl.description: Whether the server certificate is validated by the client. Default is `true`.

block.description:
Manages an SNS topic in RadosGW for bucket notifications. Topics define push endpoints where bucket event notifications are sent. Supports HTTP, AMQP 0.9.1, and Kafka endpoints.

~> **Note:** Updating a topic uses `CreateTopic` as an upsert, which replaces **all** topic attributes in a single API call. The provider automatically preserves any existing topic policy (managed by `radosgw_sns_topic_policy`) through updates. However, updating a topic may require re-creating any bucket notifications associated with it. See the [Ceph Bucket Notifications documentation](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/notifications/) for details.

~> **Ceph Reef (18.x) compatibility:** On Ceph Reef, the `GetTopicAttributes` API returns a limited set of attributes. The provider automatically preserves configured values for attributes that the API does not return (e.g., `user`, `time_to_live`, `max_retries`, `retry_sleep_duration`, and endpoint arguments). These attributes may appear empty when importing a topic on Reef.

arn.description: The ARN of the SNS topic to set the policy on.

owner.description: The owner of the SNS topic.

policy.description:
The fully-formed JSON policy document. Use `jsonencode()` or the `radosgw_iam_policy_document` data source to generate this.

Supported actions:
  - `sns:GetTopicAttributes` — list or get existing topics
  - `sns:SetTopicAttributes` — set attributes for the existing topic
  - `sns:DeleteTopic` — delete the existing topic
  - `sns:Publish` — create/subscribe notifications on the existing topic

block.description:
Manages an access policy for an SNS topic in RadosGW. The policy controls who can access the topic in addition to the owner.

~> **Note:** This resource manages the policy independently from the `radosgw_sns_topic` resource. Using both on the same topic will cause conflicts.

~> **Note:** RadosGW's `CreateTopic` API (used for topic updates) replaces all topic attributes, which would normally clear the policy. The `radosgw_sns_topic` resource handles this by reading and re-including the existing policy in every update call, so the policy managed by this resource is preserved through topic changes.

~> **Ceph version requirement:** This resource requires **Ceph Squid (19.x) or later**. The `SetTopicAttributes` API used to manage topic policies is not available on Ceph Reef (18.x).

access_key_id.description: The access key ID. For S3 keys this is the access key. For Swift keys this is `user_id:subuser`.

user.description: The user or subuser ID associated with this key. For S3 keys this is the user ID. For Swift keys this is `user_id:subuser`.

access_keys.description: List of access keys associated with the user.

id.description: The data source identifier (same as user_id).

key_type.description: Filter by key type. Valid values: `s3`, `swift`. If not specified, returns both S3 and Swift keys.

user_id.description: The user ID to retrieve access keys for.

block.description:
Retrieves information about IAM access keys associated with the specified RadosGW user. Use this data source to get S3 and/or Swift access keys for a user.

~> **Note:** The RadosGW API also returns `active` and `create_date` fields, but these are not yet exposed by the go-ceph library. They will be added in a future version when go-ceph supports them.

~> **Note:** Listing multiple S3 keys per user requires Ceph Squid (19.x) or higher. Older versions (Reef 18.x) may have issues when multiple keys exist.

arn.description: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the OIDC provider. Format: `arn:aws:iam:::oidc-provider/<url>` (URL portion excludes protocol). Exactly one of `arn` or `url` must be specified.

client_id_list.description: List of client IDs (also known as audiences) that are registered with this provider. These values correspond to the `aud` claim in OIDC tokens.

thumbprint_list.description: List of certificate thumbprints for the OpenID Connect provider's IDP certificate(s). Each thumbprint is a hex-encoded SHA-1 hash (40 characters).

url.description: URL of the identity provider. This value corresponds to the `iss` claim in OIDC tokens. Can be specified with or without the protocol prefix (`http://` or `https://`). The protocol is stripped for matching against provider ARNs. Exactly one of `arn` or `url` must be specified.

block.description:
Retrieves information about an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider in RadosGW. Use this data source to get details about an existing OIDC provider by its ARN or URL.

~> **Note:** RadosGW normalizes OIDC provider URLs by stripping the protocol (`http://`, `https://`) when constructing ARNs. This means `http://example.com` and `https://example.com` refer to the **same** OIDC provider with ARN `arn:aws:iam:::oidc-provider/example.com`. You cannot have separate providers for the same domain with different protocols.

json.description: The generated IAM policy document in JSON format.

version.description: IAM policy document version. Valid values: `2012-10-17` (default), `2008-10-17`.

actions.description: List of actions that this statement applies to (e.g., `s3:GetObject`, `s3:*`).

effect.description: Whether this statement allows or denies access. Valid values: `Allow`, `Deny`. Default: `Allow`.

not_actions.description: List of actions that this statement does NOT apply to. Use with `Allow` to create an allow-all-except policy.

not_resources.description: List of resources that this statement does NOT apply to.

resources.description: List of resources that this statement applies to (e.g., `arn:aws:s3:::bucket/*`).

values.description: Values to compare against the context key.

block.description: Condition that must be satisfied for this statement to apply.

identifiers.description: List of identifiers for the principal.

type.description: Type of principal. Valid values: `AWS`, `Federated`, `*`. Note: `Service` principals are not supported in RadosGW.

block.description: Principal to which this statement does NOT apply.

identifiers.description: List of identifiers for the principal (e.g., ARNs, account IDs, `*`).

type.description: Type of principal. Valid values: `AWS`, `Federated`, `*`. Note: `Service` principals are not supported in RadosGW.

block.description: Principal (entity) to which this statement applies.
A policy statement. Multiple statements can be specified.

Generates an IAM policy document in JSON format for use with resources that require policies, such as `radosgw_iam_role`, `radosgw_iam_role_policy`, `radosgw_s3_bucket_policy`, and `radosgw_sns_topic_policy`. This data source allows you to define policies using HCL instead of writing raw JSON.

id.description: The data source identifier in format `user_id:type`.

max_objects.description: Maximum number of objects. `-1` means unlimited.

max_size.description: Maximum size in bytes. `-1` means unlimited.

type.description:
The quota type to retrieve:
  - `user`: Total quota across all user's buckets combined
  - `bucket`: Per-bucket quota applied to each bucket the user owns

user_id.description: The user ID to retrieve quota for. Plain user IDs, tenant-qualified IDs (`tenant$user_id`), and `radosgw_iam_user.user_id` references are supported. A plain ID is used directly when a non-tenant user with that ID exists. If no direct user exists, a local tenant user ID is resolved only when it uniquely matches one tenant user. When both a global user and tenant user share the same local ID, or multiple tenants share that local ID, use `radosgw_iam_user.id` or the tenant-qualified `tenant$user_id` form.

block.description:
Retrieves user-level quota information from RadosGW.

**Important:** This data source reads quotas at the **user level**, not individual bucket quotas. There are two types:

- **User quota** (`type = "user"`): The total storage limit across ALL buckets owned by the user.

- **Bucket quota** (`type = "bucket"`): The per-bucket limit that applies to EACH bucket owned by the user.

arn.description: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the role.

assume_role_policy.description: The trust relationship policy document (in JSON format) that grants an entity permission to assume the role.

create_date.description: Date and time when the role was created, in RFC 3339 format.

max_session_duration.description: Maximum session duration (in seconds) for the role.

name.description: The name of the role to look up.

tags.description: Map of tags assigned to the role.

unique_id.description: Stable and unique string identifying the role.

block.description: Retrieves information about an existing IAM role in RadosGW. Use this data source to get role properties without having to hard code ARNs.

arns.description: Set of role ARNs matching the filter criteria.

name_regex.description: A regex pattern to filter role names. Only roles whose name matches the pattern will be returned.

names.description: Set of role names matching the filter criteria.

path_prefix.description: Path prefix for filtering the results. For example, `/application_abc/` would return all roles whose path starts with `/application_abc/`. Defaults to `/` if not specified.

block.description: Retrieves a list of IAM role names and ARNs in RadosGW. Use this data source to get all roles or filter them by path prefix or name pattern.

id.description: The data source identifier (same as user_id).
The full subuser ID in the format `{user_id}:{subuser_name}`.

name.description: The subuser name (without the parent user prefix).

subusers.description: List of subusers associated with the user.

user_id.description: The parent user ID to retrieve subusers for.

block.description:
Retrieves information about subusers associated with a RadosGW user.

Subusers are additional identities under a parent user, typically used for Swift API access. Each subuser has a full ID in the format `{user_id}:{subuser_name}`.

~> **Note:** Listing multiple subusers per user requires Ceph Squid (19.x) or higher. Older versions (Reef 18.x) may have issues when multiple subusers exist.

default_placement.description: The default placement for the user's buckets.

default_storage_class.description: The default storage class for the user's objects.

display_name.description: The display name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user.

max_buckets.description: The maximum number of buckets the user can own.

op_mask.description: The operation mask for the user (e.g., 'read, write, delete').

tenant.description: The tenant to which the user belongs.

user_id.description: The user ID to look up. For users in a tenant, use the format `tenant$user_id`.

block.description: Retrieves information about an existing RadosGW user. Use this data source to get details about a user without having to hard code user IDs.

caps.description: Set of capabilities assigned to the user.

id.description: The data source identifier (same as user_id).

user_id.description: The user ID to retrieve capabilities for.

block.description:
Retrieves the capabilities (administrative permissions) for a RadosGW user.

Capabilities control what administrative operations a user can perform. Each capability has a type (e.g., `users`, `buckets`) and a permission level (`read`, `write`, or `*`).

name_regex.description: A regex pattern to filter user IDs. Only users whose ID matches the pattern will be returned.

user_ids.description: Set of user IDs matching the filter criteria. If no filter is specified, all user IDs are returned.

block.description: Retrieves a list of RadosGW user IDs. Use this data source to get all users or filter them by a regex pattern.

bucket.description: The name of the bucket to look up.

enabled.description: Whether the bucket quota is enabled.

max_objects.description: Maximum number of objects. `-1` means unlimited.

max_size.description: Maximum size in bytes. `-1` means unlimited.

bucket_quota.description: Quota settings for this specific bucket.

creation_time.description: The creation time of the bucket in RFC3339 format.

data_extra_pool.description: The RADOS pool for storing extra object data (e.g., multipart uploads).

marker.description: The internal bucket marker used by RadosGW.

num_shards.description: The number of shards for the bucket index.

amqp_exchange.description: The AMQP exchange name (for AMQP endpoints).

arn.description: The ARN of the SNS topic.

ca_location.description: Path to the CA certificate file for SSL verification.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retries for failed deliveries. Not returned by Ceph Reef (18.x).

block.description:
Use this data source to get information about an existing SNS topic in RadosGW. By using this data source, you can reference SNS topics without having to hard code ARNs.

~> **Ceph Reef (18.x) compatibility:** On Ceph Reef, the `GetTopicAttributes` API returns a limited set of attributes. Fields such as `user`, `time_to_live`, `max_retries`, `retry_sleep_duration`, and endpoint arguments may not be populated.
